subject: Marketplace listing visibility + partner promo credit split
messages:
From: Anna Kline <anna@brightbridge.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: partners@brightbridge.com
Date: 2028-06-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Marketplace listing visibility + promo allocation

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the intro call this morning. Quick follow-up: BrightBridge is excited to list our ingestion connector in the three cloud marketplaces, but our finance and GTM teams need clarity on two items before we can proceed with the publisher intake:

1) How the marketplace catalog exposes partner logos/marketing blurbs vs. Redwood’s publisher branding.
2) How promotional credits or demo credits are allocated and reported when sales come through a marketplace private offer.

We have a small pilot POC with a mutual customer and want to coordinate a promo-credit split for joint demos. Can you share the typical splitting model (publisher:partner:cloud) you’ve used? Also attaching a short checklist of evidence the cloud will ask for.

Best,
Anna
Head of Partnerships
BrightBridge Analytics

Attachment: BrightBridge-MAAP-Promo-Terms.pdf (PDF, 230KB)

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Anna Kline <anna@brightbridge.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-18T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing visibility + promo allocation

Anna —

Great to meet earlier. Quick answers inline plus next steps.

1) Visibility: On GCP/Azure we surface the publisher line (Redwood Inference) prominently, with an optional co-sell partner tile. For AWS, the listing page supports a partner badge and a short co-sell blurb but the canonical publisher remains the list owner. There is an internal staging flag we can request that elevates your partner tile during launch week; it’s temporary but useful for demo signups.

2) Promo credits: We’ve run two common patterns:
   - Shared credit pool: Redwood issues credits to the customer and notates the deal in HubSpot; we reconcile usage and invoice partners monthly.
   - Private offer split: Cloud handles consumption credits and we exchange revenue/credit allocation via an MCF-like reconciliation (monthly CSV).

For pilots, the fastest approach is: Redwood provides demo credits against a dedicated SKU (covering token cost up to $X), BrightBridge covers the integration support time, and we split any marketplace billback 70/30 (publisher/partner) for the first 90 days, reverting to a standard 85/15 after scale.

Can Karthik and Ben weigh in on the technical gating and billing path? If that sounds OK we’ll prepare a short mutual action plan and the evidence bundle for the cloud intake.

— Olga
Head of Partner Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: BB-Marketplace-visibility-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 45KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, Anna Kline <anna@brightbridge.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-18T13:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing visibility + promo allocation

Thanks — tagging technical and intake items. Notes: 

- Evidence: Clouds will ask for an architecture diagram, multi-tenant tenancy model, data flow (no customer data persists), and SOC2 report. Anna, your team’s connector repo + deploy guide will speed things up.
- SKU strategy: We prefer a single metered SKU for ingestion and an optional demo SKU for zero-dollar crediting in private offers. The demo SKU should be non-billable and limited to a token cap.
- Metering/Reporting: For GCP/Azure, we can leverage the private offer line item with usage telemetry; for AWS, we’ll need the marketplace meter integration (monthly usage CSV).

Action items I’ll do: draft the intake form for each cloud and create a headcount/ops estimate for billing reconciliation.

Karthik
Sr. Partnerships Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Anna Kline <anna@brightbridge.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: partners@brightbridge.com
Date: 2028-06-19T08:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing visibility + promo allocation

Appreciate the clarity. Two quick asks from our side before we sign off on the mutual action plan: 

- Legal: our counsel needs the draft wording for the promo-split and a simple SOW template for pilot support (2 weeks integration + 1 month joint demo).
- Reporting cadence: can you confirm the monthly reconciliation date (e.g., 5th of each month) and whether Redwood can push a usage CSV to our finance SFTP?

If those are OK, we’ll route internally and lock the pilot timeline (target week of July 9).

— Anna

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Anna Kline <anna@brightbridge.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-20T16:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing visibility + promo allocation

Anna — quick update from commercial ops and legal: 

- Reconciliation: Redwood can run monthly reconciliations; we push a usage CSV to an SFTP endpoint by the 3rd business day of the month and net settlements within 30 days. We’ll include line-items by SKU and marketplace account id.
- Promo-split draft: attaching a one-page term sheet and a short SOW template for a two-week integration pilot.
- Visibility sprint: Olga — we can request the elevated partner tile for the launch week; need confirmation by 06/25 to schedule with the cloud listing ops team.

Next steps: Anna, if you approve the term sheet I’ll get legal to issue a simple MSA addendum + SOW, then we can submit intake to AWS/GCP/Azure in parallel.

Thanks,
Ben
Head of Partner GTM
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood-Promo-TermSheet-1pg.pdf (PDF, 18KB), RB-SOW-connector-pilot.docx (DOCX, 32KB)
